query: What signals suggest an incident resolution will be inefficient?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A clean categorization derived from short_description gives a genuine grouping axis to compare resolution efficiency across incident types. Values (network, printer, database) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: reassignment_signal
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is a strong, directly relevant signal of inefficient resolution. However, the source text (short_description + timestamps) contains no information about reassignment; assignment_group history is not shown. True/False values appear invented and are not derivable from the provided text, e.g. two near-identical 'Printer not working' rows get opposite values.

per_column.name: hardware_failure_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity could be relevant, but the column is near-constant (358/500 'functional_degradation') and is applied even to non-hardware rows (database -> functional_degradation, network -> functional_degradation), which the source text does not support. The specific severity is not warranted by brief descriptions like 'Printer not working properly'.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Reasonable extraction from short_description, though largely redundant with incident_category. Values are sound readings (printer->printer, network->network_device, database->software is a defensible inference). Adds modest leverage as an asset-level grouping.

per_column.name: shared_vs_personal_asset
per_column.rationale: Shared vs personal ownership is a plausible efficiency signal (coordination overhead). But the assignment is often an unwarranted inference: 'office printer' -> shared is reasonable, yet many rows lack any ownership cue in the text, so confident shared/personal labels are partly speculative. Unknown/<NULL> for silent rows is correct behaviour.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_signal
per_column.rationale: Repeat incidents are a strong inefficiency signal, but repeat status cannot be derived from a single row's short_description and timestamps. Values look invented: identical 'Printer is not working properly' descriptions receive True while a database issue gets False with no supporting evidence.

judge.rationale: Most columns target genuinely relevant axes for diagnosing inefficient resolution (category, reassignment, repeat, ownership), giving real grouping/modeling leverage; hardware_failure_severity is weak (near-constant, misapplied) and affected_asset_type overlaps incident_category. Groundedness is the main concern: the highest-value signals (reassignment_signal, repeat_incident_signal) and part of shared_vs_personal_asset and hardware_failure_severity assert facts not derivable from the shown source text, with contradictory values across near-identical rows. Well-grounded extraction columns (incident_category, affected_asset_type) offset this only partially.
